# torp CI pipeline

_Generated by `ops/scripts/pipeline_guide.py` from `.github/pipeline/pipeline.json`, using runs up to 22 Nov 2026, 3:07pm (Sydney time). Do not edit by hand, except the notes section: rerun the generator._

What torp's daily GitHub Actions run does, in order, and how long each part takes: it recomputes the player and team ratings from the data torpdata has just released, publishes them, then builds and publishes the AFL match predictions. When it finishes it starts torpdata's Build blog data run, which puts the results on the site's data store. This guide lives in .github/pipeline/ because the repo's docs/ folder is ignored by git (it holds the pkgdown website build).

## Daily ratings and predictions

Workflow: [`daily-ratings-predictions.yml`](https://github.com/peteowen1/torp/blob/HEAD/.github/workflows/daily-ratings-predictions.yml). Median wall time **19 min 03 s** (range 18 min 18 s to 19 min 56 s), from the first job starting to the last job ending, over the 5 run(s) listed below.

Two jobs one after the other: compute-ratings, then build-predictions. Each installs R first. Runs counted are successful ones on the main branch where both jobs succeeded and the run took over 10 minutes. The workflow on the dev branch has since gained an off-season gate job (offseason-gate) that skips scheduled runs when no match is near; it is listed below as optional because the runs counted here came from main, before it.

**What starts it, and what it starts:** In practice the four weekly pre-game schedule runs, so predictions use the published team lists: Thursday 06:00 UTC and Friday 06:00 UTC (5pm Sydney summer time), Saturday and Sunday 00:00 UTC (11am Sydney summer time); all five runs counted here were schedule runs. Also started by torpdata's Daily Data Release, which sends the ratings-trigger event after a real data release (within hours of a match ending), and by hand with Run workflow (inputs: force, week_override, seasons). When build-predictions succeeds it sends the blog-trigger event to torpdata, which starts torpdata's Build blog data run (see torpdata's guide). The two runs are not stitched together here.

### The order jobs run in

Each row is a phase: jobs in the same phase run side by side, and each phase starts when the one above it ends. Minutes and seconds are medians over the runs used; lower is better. The slowest job in each phase sets its length, so those jobs are the critical path.

| Phase | Jobs (side by side) | Median | Range | Slowest job (critical path) |
|---:|---|---:|---|---|
| 1 | compute-ratings | 9 min 39 s | 8 min 10 s to 9 min 56 s | compute-ratings |
| 2 | build-predictions | 9 min 55 s | 9 min 05 s to 10 min 10 s | build-predictions |

Critical path: compute-ratings -> build-predictions.

### Jobs

Wall time of each job, median and range over the runs used; lower is better. For a job that runs as several copies at once (a matrix), wall time is first copy starting to last copy ending, and the copies column says how many.

| Job | What it does | Copies | Median | Range | Slowest copy (median) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| compute-ratings | Rebuilds the player stat ratings, then computes the TORP ratings (player game data, EPR, team ratings, player game and season ratings, PSR) and uploads them to the torpdata releases | 1 | 9 min 39 s | 8 min 10 s to 9 min 56 s | 9 min 39 s |
| build-predictions | Trains the match models, predicts the next round, publishes the predictions and the matchup table, and tells torpdata to build the blog data | 1 | 9 min 55 s | 9 min 05 s to 10 min 10 s | 9 min 55 s |

### Steps in `compute-ratings`

Seconds each step took, in run order: median and range over the times it ran; lower is better. Share is the median step time as a percentage of the job's median time. Ran is how many of the job's runs (copies included) the step actually ran in: a step that only runs when something went wrong shows a low count.

| # | Step | What it does | Median | Range | Share | Ran |
|---:|---|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | Set up job | GitHub starts the machine and downloads the actions this job uses | 1 s | 1 s to 3 s | 0% | 5 of 5 |
| 2 | Checkout repository | Downloads this repo's code onto the machine | 3 s | 3 s to 5 s | 1% | 5 of 5 |
| 3 | Setup R | Installs R 4.4.0 | 39 s | 32 s to 49 s | 7% | 5 of 5 |
| 4 | Setup R dependencies | Installs the R packages torp needs (from a cache when it can) | 53 s | 35 s to 63 s | 9% | 5 of 5 |
| 5 | Rebuild stat ratings | Runs three scripts in data-raw/06-stat-ratings/: collects every player's per-match stats and adjusts them for the opponent, estimates each player's stat ratings round by round, and uploads the stat ratings to the torpdata release (skipped when torpdata reports a team-only release) | 2 min 19 s | 1 min 52 s to 2 min 21 s | 24% | 5 of 5 |
| 6 | Compute TORP ratings | Runs data-raw/03-ratings/run_ratings_pipeline.R: player game data, EPR ratings for the current season, team ratings, player game and season ratings, then PSR for the men's and the women's (AFLW) competitions; each stage uploads to the torpdata releases (skipped when torpdata reports a team-only release) | 5 min 34 s | 4 min 38 s to 5 min 37 s | 58% | 5 of 5 |
| 7 | Get release info | Reads the current AFL season and round | 4 s | 3 s to 6 s | 1% | 5 of 5 |
| 8 | Ratings summary | Writes the date, season, round and what started the run to the run's summary page | 0 s | 0 s to 0 s | 0% | 5 of 5 |
| 9 | Post Setup R dependencies | Clean-up for an earlier step (saves caches, removes credentials) | 4 s | 3 s to 5 s | 1% | 5 of 5 |
| 10 | Post Checkout repository | Clean-up for an earlier step (saves caches, removes credentials) | 1 s | 0 s to 1 s | 0% | 5 of 5 |
| 11 | Complete job | GitHub closes the job and cleans up the machine | 0 s | 0 s to 0 s | 0% | 5 of 5 |

#### Inside `compute-ratings`: Rebuild stat ratings, in order

Seconds each stage took, read from the job's own log (the slowest copy, for a matrix job); median and range over 5 log(s); lower is better. Each stage runs from its header line to the next one; the last runs to the end of the step.

| Stage | What it does | Median | Range | Logs |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| Loading data | Loads the per-match player stats, rosters, fixtures and lineups from torpdata | 62.5 s | 53.6 to 65.6 s | 5 |
| Preparing stat rating data | Builds one table of every player's stats for every match | 1.1 s | 1.0 to 1.1 s | 5 |
| Opponent-adjusting per-game stats | Adjusts each game's stats for the opponent, using each player's rolling past profile | 24.0 s | 16.8 to 26.9 s | 5 |
| Loading stat rating data | Reloads the prepared table for the rating step | 1.9 s | 1.0 to 2.1 s | 5 |
| Estimating stat ratings by round | Estimates every player's stat ratings round by round | 21.6 s | 20.3 to 22.6 s | 5 |
| Combining results | Joins the rounds' results into one table | 10.9 s | 8.1 to 11.7 s | 5 |
| Loading computed stat ratings | Reloads the combined ratings for export | 3.9 s | 3.1 to 4.0 s | 5 |
| Exporting to torpdata | Uploads the stat ratings to the player_stat_ratings-data release | 6.5 s | 5.1 to 8.7 s | 5 |

#### Inside `build-predictions`: Stages of the match predictions pipeline

Seconds each stage took, read from the job's own log (the slowest copy, for a matrix job); median and range over 5 log(s); lower is better. Each stage runs from its header line to the next one; the last runs to the end of the step.

| Stage | What it does | Median | Range | Logs |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| Loading data | Loads the stadium list, expected goals, fixtures, results, teams and TORP ratings from torpdata, and checks them | 42.9 s | 36.0 to 52.5 s | 5 |
| Building fixture features | Builds the fixture table from the fixture list | 0.1 s | 0.1 to 0.4 s | 5 |
| Loading PSR | Computes PSR (player stat ratings) from the released player stat ratings | 7.1 s | 6.9 to 7.9 s | 5 |
| Processing lineups | Loads the team xRAPM snapshot and builds each team's rating from its lineup | 4.3 s | 4.1 to 5.0 s | 5 |
| Computing features | Builds each match's features from the two teams' ratings and the ground | 0.1 s | 0.1 to 0.2 s | 5 |
| Loading injuries | Scrapes the current injury list | 28.6 s | 26.2 to 32.9 s | 5 |
| Loading weather | Fetches the weather | 1.3 s | 1.0 to 1.6 s | 5 |
| Building model dataset | Joins everything into one table for the models | 0.2 s | 0.2 to 0.2 s | 5 |
| Training GAM models on completed matches | Trains the GAM match models on matches already played | 175.9 s | 166.4 to 184.2 s | 5 |
| Training XGBoost models | Trains the XGBoost match models | 3.4 s | 3.2 to 4.1 s | 5 |
| Generating predictions | Predicts the coming round (matches already started keep their locked prediction) | 0.7 s | 0.6 to 1.0 s | 5 |
| Validating predictions | Checks the predictions before they are published | 0.0 s | 0.0 to 0.0 s | 5 |
| Uploading predictions | Uploads the predictions to the torpdata releases | 200.8 s | 194.2 to 215.9 s | 5 |

## How to regenerate

```
python C:/dev/ops/scripts/pipeline_guide.py build --repo-dir <this repo> --config .github/pipeline/pipeline.json
```

It reads `docs/pipeline.json` (which workflows and jobs are the pipeline, one line per step) and the latest successful runs through `gh`, saves every response raw, and rewrites this file and `docs/pipeline-summary.json`. It fails if the config names a job, step or log pattern that no longer appears, so a renamed step cannot leave a stale description behind. Steps marked **(not confirmed)** were not checked against the script they run.
